elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Client may assign or transfer this Agreement ... without the prior approval of TrueLink, to a financially responsible affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in interest by way of merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights or obligations ... without the prior written approval of Client"

elements.element: Vendor consent standard: not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "A change of control of Client shall not ... give TrueLink any right to terminate, re-price or modify this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Only "Client may assign or transfer" to a successor; TrueLink has no successor right and remains fully consent-bound
No notice obligation appears; Client assigns "without the prior approval of TrueLink" with no notice mechanic

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld"

offending_extra_words: or of the business to which this Agreement relates
and its rights and obligations hereunder
reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are present in operative text: affiliate and successor carve-outs for Client, Vendor assignment subject to Client's consent not unreasonably withheld, absolute competitor bar, and change-of-control deemed not an assignment with no Vendor termination right.
Fallback is not satisfied (no mutuality of successor right and no written-notice mechanic), but that is irrelevant since the locked target level is preferred and it is met.

Minimality fails: the whole clause was rewritten from 37 to 123 words (changed-character ratio 0.813), and the edit adds scope beyond what the preferred position requires — "reorganization", "or of the business to which this Agreement relates", "and its rights and obligations hereunder", and the extra "re-price or modify" remedies. A tighter edit adding the Client carve-out, the reasonableness/competitor qualifiers on TrueLink, and a short change-of-control sentence would suffice.
Intent preserved: the mutual-consent baseline concept survives in a party-specific form, no defined terms are broken, and no unrelated commercial term is disturbed.
